clue.text: In country businesses one must have authentic warning devices

indicators.note: the following pieces are set in the middle of the country businesses

parts.note: farms are businesses in the country

indicators.note: one is joined directly by the authentic piece, the two forming a single run

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
real means authentic, genuine

explanation.surface: Rural enterprises are told that genuine safety equipment against fire is compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts IREAL inside FARMS, after its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke-triggered bells and sirens are devices that give warning of a blaze.

clue.text: Wind in midriff? Oh, nasty!

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: Someone with a stomach ache groans about trapped gas in the belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' pretends to mean flatulence, as 'midriff' suggests; it is a weather wind. The letters run across midrifF OH Nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The föhn is a warm, dry wind blowing down the lee side of the Alps.

clue.text: "B" one is like a motorway? Yes and no!

definitions.text: "B" one is like a motorway? Yes and no!

parts.words: "B" one is like a motorway? Yes and no!
parts.note: a B-class route in Britain is a lesser highway; a motorway is one too, yet a B route is nothing like one

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a minor British route resembles a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded: motorways, A roads, then smaller B roads. Both a B road and a motorway are this, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: A B road and a motorway are both kinds of highway, the general term for a route for traffic.

clue.text: Boy with message — it comes out in film song

indicators.note: the letters emerge in a new order, as if released from their original arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad delivering a note while a tune from the movies plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out' rearranges BOY, MESSAGE and IT together.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known number sung by Dooley Wilson in Casablanca is a song from a film.

clue.text: Besieged fort taking hit with a circle gathered round

indicators.note: the letters of a and circle close round the hit, one on each side

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
lam is an informal word meaning hit or thrash

explanation.surface: A fort under siege takes a blow while a ring of attackers closes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered round' puts LAM between A and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texas mission was besieged by Mexican forces in 1836, a famous fort under siege.

clue.text: Thinks change will be accepted by fellow workers

indicators.note: the change is taken in by the fellow workers, placed within them

parts.note: mates are workmates, colleagues
to edit is to change or revise

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on whether colleagues will welcome a new way of working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow workers' are mates, British for workmates; 'change' is the verb to revise.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to ponder or reflect, which is what someone does who thinks.

clue.text: Second trophy for swimmer

parts.note: a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A runner-up prize awarded to a competitor in a swimming race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person; it is a fish, as often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The scup is a porgy, an American sea fish, so a creature that swims.

clue.text: More than one star is so epic — ace, ace, fantastic!

indicators.note: something fantastic is wildly fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
A again stands for ace

explanation.surface: An excited fan raves about a magnificent performance with enthusiastic superlatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges ISSOEPIC with one A; the second A ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: This W-shaped northern constellation is made up of several stars, more than a single one.

clue.text: Agreeable comment from Left swallowed by poor workers

indicators.note: the letter for Left is taken inside the poor workers as if eaten

parts.note: the peasantry are poor agricultural labourers as a class

explanation.surface: A political remark from the Left goes down well with the labouring poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed by' puts L inside PEASANTRY, after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant, polite or joking remark is an agreeable comment.

clue.text: Earls hadn't abandoned central territory

indicators.note: letters thrown into disorder, as in abandoned, unrestrained behaviour

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Noblemen had not yet deserted their estates in the middle of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like a verb about land; it signals rearranging EARLS and HADNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartlands are the central, core regions of a country or area.

clue.text: Actual existence of fairies, seemingly

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the following words, spanning their join

explanation.surface: A sceptical remark on whether fairies really exist, judging by appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fairiES SEemingly. The answer is a Latin philosophical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy the Latin word for 'to be' names real being, the fact of existing.

clue.text: No chalet menu could supply this processed food

indicators.note: the letters of the words are reworked to provide something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ski chalet with no menu offers only tinned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could supply' rearranges NOCHALETMENU.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam-style tinned pork is a processed food made of ground, pressed meat.

clue.text: Tourism Dept I run to get money from foreign countries

indicators.note: to run the letters is to put them through a process that rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An official boasts of managing a government tourism office that earns foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' rearranges TOURISMDEPTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs levied on goods brought in from abroad are money raised from foreign countries' trade.

clue.text: I close form naughtily engaged in pranks

indicators.note: behaving badly, the letters misbehave and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher shuts a class that has behaved badly, playing tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' rearranges ICLOSEFORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful and full of high spirits describes someone given to larks and practical jokes.

clue.text: Start to suffer with muscle? Then get one of the top people, hospital expert

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle
I is the Roman numeral for one
the A-list is the most important or celebrated people

explanation.surface: A patient with a muscle injury is told to see a top hospital consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the top people' is the A-list, the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant concentrating on one branch of medicine is an expert in a hospital.

clue.text: Offensive ruling when revolutionary university president is installed

indicators.note: the turned pair is set into the ruling word

parts.note: regnant means reigning, ruling

indicators.note: turned round, so university and president are read backwards

explanation.surface: A rebel academic made head of the state is a hateful ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the university and president letters round; 'is installed' sets them in the Latin-derived word for reigning.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means repellent or distasteful, causing offence.

clue.text: B&B's central feature

parts.note: the character between the two Bs of B&B, rather than the breakfast or the beds a guesthouse offers

explanation.surface: What makes a bed and breakfast stand out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: B&B is short for a bed-and-breakfast guesthouse; read literally, the middle character is the '&' sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The '&' symbol meaning 'and' sits in the middle of the abbreviation B&B.

clue.text: Chicken in pot inside another container

indicators.note: the pot goes within the other container

parts.note: a can is a container
a po is a chamber pot

explanation.surface: A cook puts a chicken in a pot and then that pot in a bigger vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is the chamber pot, informally a po in British English, not a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a kind of chicken.

clue.text: Something attractive about cold brass

indicators.note: the attractive thing goes round the cold letter

parts.note: a lure is a bait, something that attracts
C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps

explanation.surface: A magnet-like ornament placed around a chilly brass fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is British slang for money, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both slang brass and filthy lucre are words for money, especially gained dishonestly.

clue.text: Bill, one getting nothing right, is bottom

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck up in public
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man called Bill, with nothing going right, finishes last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The posterior is the backside or buttocks, colloquially the bottom.

clue.text: Court officials in rows crossing yellow line

indicators.note: the rows reach across and enclose the yellow and the line

parts.note: chains are rows or series of linked things
amber is a yellow colour

explanation.surface: Royal officers in a queue step over a yellow road marking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow line' suggests a British parking restriction, but the colour and the line are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlains manage the household of a sovereign or noble, officials of the royal court.

clue.text: Mayonnaise is excellent, containing unusual oil

indicators.note: the excellent letters hold the shuffled oil

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate, excellent

indicators.note: out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook praises a mayonnaise made with an exotic oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the oil; 'excellent' is A1, written with an I as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal garlic mayonnaise.

clue.text: There's something wicked about a Welsh girl

indicators.note: the wicked thing surrounds the article

parts.note: a transgression or wicked deed, the three-letter word for wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl has a naughty secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Siân is a common Welsh girl's name, a Welsh form of Jane.

clue.text: Worker getting energy from what is put down on table?

definitions.text: what is put down on table?

parts.note: a worker ant is the standard crossword ant
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A labourer gets a boost from a meal laid on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like setting a dish down; it is a poker stake placed on the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player's stake, placed before the deal, is money put down on the gaming table.

clue.text: Miss nothing, having joined American university

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A diligent student at an American university never skips a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a title; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to fail to include it, as when one misses a line.

clue.text: Hour man needs to collect a series of deliveries in royal house

indicators.note: the hour and the man take in the other pieces between them

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
an is the indefinite article, a
an over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A postman must pick up several parcels at a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to collect' puts ANOVER between H and IAN. An over is cricket's run of six balls from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanoverian dynasty ruled Britain from George I to Victoria, a royal house.

clue.text: Trading organisation featured in the FT advertisement

indicators.note: the letters appear within the words, running across them

explanation.surface: A trade bloc places an advert in the Financial Times.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across thE FT Advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Free Trade Association is a trading bloc of non-EU European states.

clue.text: Permission to enter a social event — Romney gains access

indicators.note: the man gets into the social event, inside its letters

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering
Mitt Romney is the American politician

explanation.surface: An American politician is let into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gains access' puts MITT inside ADANCE after its AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is the right or permission to go into a place.
